- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to catch downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward 1–2 days later.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — if price is trending sharply, forecast should not revert too quickly; allow 2–3 day lag in correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period corrections; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative in last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for potential rebound.
